newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends down on poor demand, gilts steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends down on poor demand, gilts steady.

text.p: Indian call money rates fell on Thursday on lack of demand to end in the 7.0-7.5 percent range against the day's opening 10.0-10.25 percent, dealers said.
They said there were stray deals around three percent.
"Rates fell sharply on lack of demand as it is the last day for covering," a dealer said. "Banks had covered their positions and there was little demand for funds."
Banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India on Friday.
Dealers said prices of government securities were largely steady in dull trade. "The undertone is weak," said a dealer. "There was not much trade today."
The 13.85 percent 2001 government of India stock was traded on Thursdy at 101.70 rupees against its last traded price of 101.68 rupees, dealers said.
Commercial paper maturing in February 1997 was traded at a yield of 11.60 percent, they said.
